note: Arabic means 'was able to succeed thanks to your help'; use a natural equivalent that preserves the original B-band progression.
proposed_target: استطعت أن أنجح بفضل مساعدتك.
proposed_english: Your help enabled me to succeed.

note: Missing hamzas in أحب and أفعل.
proposed_target: هذا ما أحب أن أفعله.
proposed_english: This is what I love to do.

note: Standard learner-facing orthography uses غدًا.
proposed_target: غدًا هو أول يوم عمل لي.
proposed_english: Tomorrow is my first day of work.

note: Arabic says 'repeat this tomorrow'; English paraphrases it as 'do this again tomorrow'.
proposed_target: علينا تكرار هذا غدًا.
proposed_english: We have to repeat this tomorrow.

note: تسألني للمساعدة is an unnatural calque for 'ask me for help'.
proposed_target: يمكنك دائمًا أن تطلب مني المساعدة.
proposed_english: You can always ask me for help.

note: العودة means return; English 'go home' loses that meaning.
proposed_target: يمكنك العودة إلى البيت لو أردت.
proposed_english: You can return home if you like.

note: يمكنك أنت تقول is ungrammatical; after يمكنك use أن تقول.
proposed_target: يمكنك أن تقول أي شيء تريد.
proposed_english: You can say whatever you want to.

note: يمكنك is 'can', not conditional 'could'.
proposed_target: يمكنك المجيء والعيش معي.
proposed_english: You can come and live with me.

note: كأن عليك means roughly 'as if you have to'; it does not express past counterfactual 'ought to have come'.
proposed_target: كان ينبغي أن تأتي إلى هنا مبكرًا.
proposed_english: You ought to have come here earlier.

note: Arabic لنجاحنا corresponds to 'for our success', not 'to our success'.
proposed_target: مساعدتك ضرورية لنجاحنا.
proposed_english: Your help is necessary for our success.

note: تجرء is misspelled; present 'dare' is تجرؤ. Match exclamatory punctuation.
proposed_target: كيف تجرؤ على قول شيء كهذا!
proposed_english: How dare you say such a thing!

note: تسمع means hear; English requires deliberate listening.
proposed_target: كل ما عليك فعله هو أن تستمع بعناية.
proposed_english: All you need to do is listen carefully.

note: شاكر لمساعدتك لي is awkward learner-facing MSA; use idiomatic ممتن ... على.
proposed_target: أنا ممتن لك على مساعدتك.
proposed_english: I am grateful to you for your help.

note: Current Arabic says 'I thought you called me for that'; rewrite to match the causal English precisely.
proposed_target: افترضت أن هذا هو سبب اتصالك بي.
proposed_english: I assumed that was why you called me.

note: Arabic says 'I don't know how to thank you for this help', not the idiom 'cannot thank you enough'.
proposed_target: لا أجد كلمات تكفي لشكرك على مساعدتك.
proposed_english: I cannot thank you enough for your assistance.

note: Arabic says 'I don't think I know this place'; English says 'where that is'.
proposed_target: لا أعتقد أنني أعرف هذا المكان.
proposed_english: I don't think I know this place.

note: Arabic explicitly says ما يكفي من الوقت ('enough time'); English omits 'enough'.
proposed_target: لا أعلم إن كان لدي ما يكفي من الوقت.
proposed_english: I don't know if I have enough time.

note: الباص is colloquial/loan-register; use standard MSA الحافلة.
proposed_target: لا أدري أين موقف الحافلة.
proposed_english: I don't know where the bus stop is.

note: Bare لم is ambiguous here and English adds 'just', absent from Arabic. Make first-person subject explicit.
proposed_target: لا أعلم لماذا فعلتُ ذلك.
proposed_english: I don't know why I did that.

note: تنساني means 'forget me'; English adds 'about'.
proposed_target: لا أريدك أن تنساني.
proposed_english: I don't want you to forget me.

note: لأنهي واجبي means 'to finish my homework', not merely 'do'.
proposed_target: لدي أسبوع لأنهي واجبي.
proposed_english: I have a week to finish my homework.

note: Arabic does not explicitly contain 'with me'.
proposed_target: ليس لدي أكثر من 1,000 ين.
proposed_english: I have no more than 1,000 yen.

note: Arabic says words cannot express the speaker's thanks; English uses a different construction.
proposed_target: الكلمات لا يمكنها أن تعبر عن شكري لك.
proposed_english: Words cannot express my gratitude to you.

note: Missing hamzas and standard spelling in أعلم بأنه ليس لدي أي فرصة.
proposed_target: أعلم بأنه ليس لدي أي فرصة للفوز.
proposed_english: I know I have no chance of winning.

note: يجب أن أعرف is 'I have to/must know', stronger and more exact than 'need to know'.
proposed_target: يجب أن أعرف لماذا تحتاج هذا.
proposed_english: I have to know why you need this.

note: Missing hamzas; الآن means 'now' while English says 'right away'. Use حالًا for exact urgency.
proposed_target: أحتاج أن أتحدث معك حالًا.
proposed_english: I need to speak with you right away.

note: Missing hamzas in أعتقد أن.
proposed_target: أعتقد أن الحياة هي ما تصنعه.
proposed_english: I think life is what you make it.

note: Arabic says الذهاب معي ('go with me'); English 'come along' is less exact.
proposed_target: ظننت أنك قد تود الذهاب معي.
proposed_english: I thought you might want to go with me.

note: أودّ means 'I would like', not simple 'I want'.
proposed_target: أودّ معرفة سبب فعلك لذلك.
proposed_english: I would like to know why you did that.

note: وقت أكثر لي is understandable but awkward learner-facing MSA; use an idiomatic phrase for time spent together.
proposed_target: أتمنى لو كان لديك وقت أطول تقضيه معي.
proposed_english: I wish you had more time for me.
